corrections.text: The article contrasts "Meta's card" (Beam 80.1 versus Muse Spark Open 76.4 on Terminal-Bench 2.1) with Artificial Analysis as the independent reference, and says the sources do not explain the gap between Meta's 76.4 and Ricursive's 78.7. The Muse Spark Open model card links "our report" to Meta's "Muse Spark Open Evaluation Methodology" (October 2026), which the article does not cite. That document says Meta took the Terminal-Bench 2.1 results for every model except Beam from Artificial Analysis, using the Terminus 2 agent harness in an E2B sandbox, and used Beam's self-reported figure, for which the harness is not specified. The 76.4 is therefore an Artificial Analysis-sourced result compiled in Meta's table, not a score Meta ran itself.

The article says Meta's card lists an Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index of 39 for Muse Spark Open "without naming an index version", and cites SiliconANGLE for Meta saying a full evaluation report is still to come. The methodology document linked from the card names the index as Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v4.3 (ten evaluations), with scores sourced from Artificial Analysis on October 7, 2026, while the Artificial Analysis page the article cites gives 25 under version 5.0.1 (nine evaluations). The 39 and the 25 therefore come from different index versions. Whether the linked document is the full evaluation report SiliconANGLE described is not established.
